questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The university had some recommendations. But very expensive -9000kr/month

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It gives you more freedom as you don't have to follow the on-campus rules. Also, ensure that the leasing agency accepts payments from foreign banks or that fees may be added.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *

questions.answer: I had a person I could email

questions.answer: I got everything I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register long before your stay as availability decreases fast.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was about the same as in my home country (Denmark).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses are graded on every assignment and not only a final exam. We were also given points for answering questions correctly during the lectures.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Instrument analysis, Biochemistry laboratory, Modern biophysical methods, Advanced inorganic chemistry.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Instrument analysis and Biochemistry laboratory. I learned a lot from these courses and did not have a huge workload

questions.answer: pretty easy if you speak English well.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Tipping was pretty annoying

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People seem to be very health conscious and active. I also liked the sense of freedom that comes with everyone owning a car.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
-Make sure you have enough money saved up Boulder is expensive (cost me about 100k dkk total). 
-Choose courses with low workload so you have time for other things Americans expect you to work more hours than Danes
-If you can, find a car. There is not much to do in Boulder but a lot in Denver

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure your courses are in the same building if they are right after each other

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to meet the American people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the paperwork

questions.answer: Yes
